claims.text: Controlled aging can induce coherent Ti–Ni intermetallic precipitates in a Ti–Ni-primary high-entropy alloy.
The aging-induced precipitates increase elevated-temperature yield strength.
The aging-induced precipitates improve creep resistance by reducing creep rate.
The initial Ti–Ni-primary alloy can be prepared as a homogenized, single-phase solid solution.
Titanium and nickel are the primary constituents of the proposed alloy.
Every constituent of the proposed high-entropy alloy is constrained to 5–35 at%.
A multicomponent composition in the stated concentration range produces high configurational entropy.
A solution treatment will homogenize the proposed Ti–Ni-primary alloy.
Aging at 700–850°C for 1–4 hours will promote precipitate nucleation and growth in the proposed alloy.
The resulting precipitates will be coherent, nanoscale, and uniformly distributed in the Ti–Ni-dominated matrix.
The precipitates obstruct dislocation motion through precipitation strengthening.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by the precipitates enhances yield strength at elevated temperature.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by the precipitates reduces elevated-temperature creep rate.
The intervention is expected to remain effective at operating temperatures up to approximately 900°C.
The effectiveness of the treatment depends on compositional stability and controlled aging parameters.
The proposed comparison uses samples of identical alloy composition that differ in whether they receive the targeted aging treatment.
A result with less than a 10% yield-strength increase and no measurable creep-rate reduction is specified as a falsifying outcome.

contradictions.description: The baseline is defined as a homogeneous single-phase alloy without targeted aging, but the experiment permits an as-cast comparator as an alternative to a solution-treated comparator. An as-cast sample may differ in homogenization and phase state as well as aging, so it is not necessarily the stated baseline or a control differing only by the intervention.
